sources.title: National Climate Resilience Assessment for Algeria
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate and infrastructure evidence through 2024; projections to 2081–2100.
sources.methodology: IEA assessment combines climate observations, IPCC projections, INFORM hazard indicators and energy-system exposure analysis.
sources.limitations: Most infrastructure examples concern energy assets; household vulnerability is not comprehensively mapped.

sources.title: Inclusive insurance and risk financing in Algeria: Snapshot and way forward 2023
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Insurance and Risk Finance Facility and UNDP Algeria
sources.temporal_coverage: Hazard records range from historical periods through 2020; insurance and disaster-finance snapshot mainly covers 2019–2021.
sources.methodology: The 23-page summary presents an inclusive-insurance and disaster-risk-finance country diagnostic and key hazard impacts.
sources.limitations: Historical hazard and insurance data are dated, not a current local assessment.

sources.title: Algeria: Selected Issues, Fiscal Reforms to Support Addressing Climate Change Challenges
sources.temporal_coverage: IMF staff climate-risk and fiscal analysis completed in March 2024; includes projections through 2100 and policy simulations.
sources.methodology: IMF staff assesses physical and fiscal climate risks and models policy options using the IMF-World Bank Climate Policy Assessment Tool.
sources.limitations: Impact pathways and policy results are projections or model outputs; they do not establish observed displacement or violence.

sources.title: Urban Natural Hazard Vulnerability Reduction Project: Technical Annex to the Memorandum of the President
sources.temporal_coverage: Technical annex and proposed project design following the November 2001 Algiers flood.
sources.methodology: Technical annex documents local vulnerability diagnoses, project components, institutional arrangements and intended emergency works.
sources.limitations: This is a 2002 design-stage annex; proposed surveys, training and protections are not evidence of completed results.

sources.title: Law No. 24-04 of 26 February 2024 on prevention, intervention and reduction of disaster risks
sources.organization: Official Gazette of the People's Democratic Republic of Algeria
sources.temporal_coverage: Statutory disaster-risk governance provisions published March 2024.
sources.methodology: Official Gazette publishes the French translation of Law 24-04 and its disaster-risk governance requirements.
sources.limitations: Statutory mandates do not establish whether local plans, training or warning systems operate effectively.

claims.locator: IEA assessment, 'Other climate risks,' September 2024 flood event
claims.paraphrase: The assessment reports September 2024 flooding displaced 280 families in Béchar and damaged roads and electricity infrastructure in southern and western Algeria.
claims.limitations: The assessment reports event impacts but does not attribute this flood to climate change.

claims.locator: IEA assessment, 'Temperature,' regional heat exposure comparison for 1995–2014
claims.paraphrase: Across 1995–2014, 14 coastal wilayas recorded 20–39 days annually above 35°C, versus 112–161 days in seven southern Saharan wilayas.
geographies: seven southern wilayas in the Sahara
claims.limitations: The assessment gives regional ranges, not values for individual named wilayas or population-level exposure.

claims.paraphrase: IEA projects lower precipitation in northern populated regions under both assessed scenarios, while the south could receive up to 71% more rainfall in the high-warming case.
claims.scenario: Below 2°C and Above 3°C global-warming scenarios; projection period 2081–2100.
claims.limitations: Regional climate projections do not identify local impacts or household-level consequences.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. 5, 'Key risks and hazards,' Drought
claims.paraphrase: The diagnostic identifies the high cereal plains and pre-Saharan steppe pastures as drought-sensitive; it records a 1999–2002 drought and losses in 2013.
institutions: UNDP Insurance and Risk Finance Facility
claims.limitations: The summary states that the 1999–2002 drought could have been linked to climate change; attribution is uncertain.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. 5, 'Key risks and hazards,' Floods
claims.paraphrase: It reports nearly 300,000 people affected by 42 major floods in 1980–2020, affecting dense urban populations and rural farmers.
affected_groups: nearly 300,000 people affected across recorded events
institutions: UNDP Insurance and Risk Finance Facility
claims.limitations: The summary does not give a municipality-by-municipality distribution for these 42 events.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. 5, 'Key risks and hazards,' Storms
claims.paraphrase: The diagnostic says coastal storms particularly affect the Oran coastline, damaging port infrastructure, maritime transport and aquaculture farms.
institutions: UNDP Insurance and Risk Finance Facility
claims.limitations: No event dates, loss totals or affected-person counts are given.

claims.locator: PDF printed pp. 3 and 6, key messages on insurance and disaster-risk finance
claims.paraphrase: In its 2023 snapshot, UNDP found inclusive insurance virtually absent; the State funded over 99% of disaster costs, local insurers covered under 1%, and no sovereign risk-transfer mechanism was used.
affected_groups: households and firms exposed to natural disasters
claims.limitations: These figures describe the diagnostic period, not current coverage after 2023.

claims.paraphrase: IMF staff says lower farm productivity may harm jobs and incomes; water/food insecurity, disasters and harsher conditions may displace people and pressure northern-coast infrastructure and resources.
claims.scenario: No specific emissions scenario is stated for the displacement-risk passage.
claims.limitations: Projected pathway, not measured displacement or violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: IMF links climate-related livelihood/basic-needs stress to displacement and northern-coast resource pressure.

claims.locator: IMF report, printed p. 21, paragraph 32, fiscal-space policy options
claims.paraphrase: IMF staff models that reducing the fossil-fuel price gap by one-third could raise average annual revenue by 7% of GDP over a decade, with space for targeted transfers and adaptation investment.
claims.scenario: Fossil-fuel price gap reduced by one-third; IMF estimates average annual revenues of 7% of GDP over the next decade.
claims.limitations: This is a modeled policy option, not an adopted or delivered fiscal measure.

claims.locator: Technical Annex, section 2.1, studies of vulnerable Algiers sites
claims.paraphrase: Annex names Hamiz Oued, Oued El Harrach, Ouchaiah Oued, Kniss Oued and Telemly for a flood, landslide, seismic and pollution study; it proposes separate catchment-basin work for Bouzareah.
claims.limitations: The list was tentative; the annex says detailed study would set priorities and provides no final site-risk ranking.

claims.locator: Technical Annex, section 1, response to November 2001 flooding
claims.paraphrase: After the 2001 Algiers flood, the Wilaya of Algiers and public agencies, administrations and residents provided emergency measures and temporary relief that partly mitigated immediate impacts.
claims.limitations: The annex describes immediate relief but does not evaluate longer-term recovery or response effectiveness.

claims.locator: Technical Annex, section 2.1–2.2, institutional studies and training
claims.paraphrase: The project design proposed a meteorological monitoring and early-warning system in Algiers for possible national expansion and training for civil protection, water-resources and meteorology agencies.
claims.limitations: These are design-stage activities; the annex does not verify their implementation or present-day operation.

claims.paraphrase: The law requires risk analysis at site, commune, wilaya, inter-wilaya and national scales, with warning levels at national, local and site levels, plus local training and prevention plans.
claims.limitations: The law establishes statutory requirements; it does not establish that each plan or warning level is functioning.

search_audit.query: Algeria municipality wilaya climate vulnerabilities flood drought wildfire report local adaptation
search_audit.outcome: Opened reports with named evidence for Béchar, Oran and Algiers sites, plus distinct drought, flood and heat vulnerabilities in broad agricultural, coastal and southern zones.

search_audit.query: Algeria climate security social discontent food insecurity displacement climate risk IMF report
search_audit.outcome: The IMF report explicitly identifies potential climate-linked livelihood stress and displacement toward the northern coast; no source established an observed climate-caused conflict or violence event.

search_audit.query: Algeria conflict insecurity disrupting adaptation disaster response climate services report
search_audit.outcome: No Algeria-specific source linked conflict or insecurity to impaired adaptation or climate-service delivery. Regional North Africa material was not used as country evidence; this remains an evidence gap.

search_audit.query: Algeria early warning municipal disaster risk management capacity law 24-04 insurance
search_audit.outcome: Opened the official disaster-risk law, the historical World Bank Algiers project annex, and UNDP's risk-finance diagnostic; legal mandates and project plans are separated from demonstrated operations.

gaps: No existing DZA country baseline was present in the worktree.
The IMF climate-to-displacement pathway is projected risk framing, not measured migration, intergroup tension or conflict.
No country-specific evidence was found that conflict or insecurity has disrupted climate adaptation or service delivery; this is not evidence of absence.
The National Climate Plan PDF exceeded web extraction size limits and its Ministry download page timed out; no claims rely on search snippets.
IEA heat ranges cover unnamed groups of coastal and southern wilayas; the report does not provide named-wilaya values in the cited passage.
The 2002 World Bank annex documents intended studies and training but not implementation results.
